answer.text: Government-issued currency not backed by a physical commodity like gold
Currency backed by gold reserves held by the central bank
Digital currency issued by a private institution
Currency whose value is determined by a fixed peg to another currency

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 13, fiat money is government-issued currency not backed by a physical commodity such as gold or silver. Its value derives from supply and demand and from the stability of the issuing government. Most modern paper currencies, including USD and INR, are fiat currencies. The Trap: Gold-backed currency belongs to the gold-standard era, not modern fiat money. Note: Page 13 ties fiat value to supply/demand and issuing-government stability, with USD and INR cited as examples.
